name: OK-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+28 partisan lean in a rural Oklahoma district
Incumbent Josh Brecheen running for reelection
Democratic challenger raised only about $4,300 with $86 on hand
Prediction markets price Republican win at 98%
model.rationale: The district's R+28 lean, Brecheen's incumbency, and the challenger's negligible fundraising all point to an easy Republican hold, and markets agree at 98% for the GOP. No polls or expert ratings exist, but nothing in the evidence suggests movement away from a Safe R rating.
model.watch: Any late surge in Democratic fundraising or outside spending would be the only realistic signal of a competitive race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Josh Brecheen, the Republican incumbent in this heavily Republican southeastern Oklahoma district, is favored to win reelection easily. The district's partisan lean of roughly 28 points to the right, combined with his incumbency advantage, makes a Democratic upset highly unlikely. His challenger, Brandon Wade, has raised only about $4,300 and reports just $86 on hand, while Brecheen has raised nearly $219,000. An independent candidate, Ronnie Hopkins, is also on the ballot but shows no measurable campaign activity. Prediction markets give the Republican about a 98% chance of winning. With no public polls and no expert ratings targeting the race, the forecast rests on fundamentals, which uniformly favor the incumbent. The race is rated Safe Republican.
